metadata.title: Leave the camera alone unless a selection extends beyond the view
metadata.summary: Committing an analysis-area selection used to fit the map with a maxZoom: 5 ceiling, clamping every commit out to a multi-state view. The camera now moves only when the selection does not already fit, and when it stays put the Analyze/Cancel tooltip is anchored so it cannot land off-screen.

overview.purpose: The MMGIS-side wrapper for the AOI plugin. It owns the panel's state, bridges the React UI to the map over the mmgisAPI event bus, and funnels a selection from any of the four sources (search, draw, boundary click, upload) into a map layer, an emitted event, and the Analyze/Cancel tooltip.
overview.background: MMGIS plugins never touch the map engine directly. They `request` named providers on a bus that `Map_.js` registers against whichever engine is active — Leaflet, deck.gl overlaid on a MapLibre basemap, or standalone deck.gl — and subscribe to re-emitted engine events such as `map:moveend`. Every request returns a promise, so anything that depends on the map's answer has to be written as a chain.

keyPieces.name: _applySelection
keyPieces.description: The single funnel every selection source ends in: draws the selection layer, emits areaDrawn, decides the camera move, mounts the tooltip.

keyPieces.name: _showTooltip
keyPieces.description: Mounts the Analyze/Cancel tooltip as a map overlay anchored to one lat/lng.

keyPieces.name: _onSearchSelect / _onDrawComplete / _onMapFeatureClick / _onUploadFile
keyPieces.description: The four entry points, all of which hand off to _applySelection — so one camera rule covers all of them.

explanations.title: Declare the new bus dependency
explanations.what: The plugin's declared requests gain `map:getBounds` alongside `map:fitBounds`.
explanations.why: This header block is the plugin's contract with the core, and the selection path now asks what is currently on screen before deciding whether to move the camera at all.

explanations.title: Move the decisions into helpers
explanations.what: Imports two new pure helpers, `selectionFitBounds` and `selectionTooltipAnchor`.
explanations.why: Both decisions are geometry rather than map plumbing. As pure functions over a bbox and a view they can be tested against the antimeridian and rotation cases without standing up a map engine — which is what the new spec file at the end of this review does.

explanations.title: Make the tooltip anchor view-aware
explanations.what: `showTooltip` now takes the current view and routes the centroid through `selectionTooltipAnchor` instead of using it raw.
explanations.why: The tooltip is mounted through `map:addOverlay` at a fixed lat/lng and carries the selection's only Analyze and Cancel buttons. Now that the camera often does not move, an off-screen centroid would put those buttons somewhere the user cannot reach.
explanations.impact: Whether a `view` argument is passed is what encodes "the camera did not move" — that is the thing to track through the two call sites below.

explanations.title: Ask the view before moving
explanations.what: The path now requests `map:getBounds` first and asks `selectionFitBounds` whether a move is needed; a null answer mounts the tooltip straight away and issues no camera call.
explanations.why: The old code fitted unconditionally with `padding: 120, maxZoom: 5`, and maxZoom is a ceiling — so every selection, however small, was clamped out to roughly a multi-state view. For a shape the user drew inside a viewport they deliberately set up, the correct move is none.
explanations.impact: A failed `getBounds` degrades to `null`, which the helper treats as "view unknown" and fits — the old behavior minus the bad ceiling. The guard gains `api?.request` because the path now leads with a request rather than an event subscription.

explanations.title: Defer the tooltip only when fitting
explanations.what: The `moveend` one-shot, its 1500ms fallback and the `fitBounds` call all move inside the branch that actually fits, and the rejection path hands the unchanged view back to `settle`.
explanations.why: Waiting on `moveend` only makes sense when a move was ordered; on the no-move path — now the common one — the tooltip would otherwise have sat behind the full fallback timer before appearing.
explanations.impact: The payload `oneShot` throws away comes from `Map_.js`, which re-emits the engine's own `moveend` verbatim onto the bus. Wiring `settle` to the event directly would therefore hand a view state into the `ViewBounds` slot the anchor helper reads, and the tooltip would be placed off a shape that has no corners.

explanations.title: Terminal catch on the camera chain
explanations.what: A final `.catch` closes the promise chain.
explanations.why: Anything thrown inside the `.then` — a malformed bounds shape from some engine, say — would otherwise surface as an unhandled rejection and silently leave the selection with no tooltip.

overview.purpose: Pure helpers behind the AOI plugin: parsing uploaded GeoJSON/KML/shapefiles, building the boundary search index, deriving a feature's centroid and bbox — and now deciding whether a committed selection needs a camera move and where its tooltip belongs.
overview.background: `featureBounds` is a raw min/max sweep over every vertex, so a MultiPolygon with parts either side of ±180 — Alaska in the bundled state boundaries — reports a bbox about 359° wide rather than the ~40° the shape occupies. Longitude comparisons here have to survive that as well as the several ways the engines spell a view.

keyPieces.name: featureBounds / featureCentroid
keyPieces.description: Existing naive sweeps over a feature's vertices; the source of the pathological Alaska extent the new code has to absorb.

keyPieces.name: selectionFitBounds
keyPieces.description: Returns a map:fitBounds payload, or null meaning leave the camera alone.

keyPieces.name: selectionTooltipAnchor
keyPieces.description: Returns where to mount the tooltip, falling back to the view centre when the centroid is off-screen.

explanations.title: Pin down what the engines report
explanations.what: Declares the `ViewBounds` shape every `map:getBounds` producer returns, and a `wrap360` fold.
explanations.why: There is no shared type for this in the codebase: `Map_.js` forwards whatever the active adapter's `getBounds()` returns. Writing the union of those three behaviors down here is what lets the functions below be plain arithmetic — and one of the three producers is the standalone deck.gl path this same PR rewrites.

explanations.title: Measure eastward from the west edge
explanations.what: `viewLngExtent` gives a view's width in degrees measured east from its `southWest.lng`; `lngOffset` gives how far east of that edge a longitude sits.
explanations.why: Choosing the west edge as the origin is what collapses the wrapped and unwrapped spellings of the same window into one answer, so neither function below needs to know which engine produced the view or how it happened to be phrased.

explanations.title: Decide whether to move the camera
explanations.what: Returns null when the bbox already fits the view or its extent cannot be framed, and otherwise a `map:fitBounds` payload with `padding: 40` and `maxZoom: 18`.
explanations.why: Those two numbers are the direct replacement for the `padding: 120, maxZoom: 5` that AOITool used to send unconditionally — the ceiling raised until it can no longer bind on a real selection, and the padding cut to a margin rather than a zoom level's worth of it. Everything else here is about not making the camera worse than leaving it alone.
explanations.impact: The issue asks for "no further than containing the selection requires", and this is the only place that promise is enforced; any future caller that wants a different framing should pass different options rather than widen these.

explanations.title: Keep the tooltip reachable
explanations.what: Returns the centroid when it falls inside the supplied view or when no view is supplied, and the centre of the view otherwise.
explanations.why: This exists because the two functions are used together: the moment `selectionFitBounds` started answering "do nothing", the centroid stopped being guaranteed on-screen, and the tooltip is the only way to act on a selection at all. The absent-view argument is the caller's way of saying the camera was fitted.
explanations.impact: The fallback deliberately re-centres rather than clamping to an edge, so the tooltip cannot end up half off the map on a selection that is only just outside the view.

overview.purpose: Implements MMGIS's engine-agnostic `IMapEngine` interface on top of deck.gl, in two modes: overlaid on a MapLibre basemap that owns the camera, or standalone, where deck owns the view state itself.
overview.background: Standalone mode has no basemap to ask for geographic bounds, so it derives them by unprojecting container pixel coordinates through a `WebMercatorViewport` built from the current view state — which carries bearing and pitch, because drag-rotate is enabled. The branch's last commit also reworded existing comments in this file for plainer English; those hunks change no behavior.

keyPieces.name: getBounds
keyPieces.description: Backs the map:getBounds bus provider the AOI selection path now depends on.

explanations.title: Wording-only docblock rewrites
explanations.what: Existing comments restated in plainer English, with no code change.
explanations.why: The same rewrite touches several other blocks further down this file — `setBasemapStyle`, `bringToFront`, `bringToBack`, `_anchorBelowDrawing`, `_sortLayersByZIndex` — none of which are part of the selection-camera change and can be skimmed on the same basis.

explanations.title: Envelope all four corners
explanations.what: Standalone `getBounds` now unprojects all four container corners and takes the min and max across them, instead of reading the bottom-left and top-right pixels as south-west and north-east.
explanations.why: This is why a rendering adapter appears in a PR about a plugin's camera: `getBounds` was only ever used loosely before, and the AOI containment check is the first caller that depends on its corners being ordered. Under rotation they were not, so the plugin read on-screen selections as out of view and off-screen ones as contained.
explanations.impact: Under pitch the north-up envelope overstates the extent toward the horizon, so a selection just past the top edge can read as contained. That errs toward leaving the camera alone, which is the bias this whole change wants.

overview.purpose: New unit coverage for the selection camera behavior: the two pure helpers on their own, and `_applySelection`'s wiring of them against a mocked bus.
overview.background: Vitest with jsdom. `_applySelection` reaches the map only through `window.mmgisAPI`, so the entire path can be driven by a mock that records the requests it receives — no engine, no DOM map. `AOITool` is a module singleton, which is why teardown has to reset its state.

keyPieces.name: view / ALASKA_BBOX / squareFeature
keyPieces.description: Shared fixtures: an asymmetric current view, the real bundled Alaska extent, and a rectangle factory.

keyPieces.name: mockApi
keyPieces.description: Installs a window.mmgisAPI whose request() records every call and answers map:getBounds with a supplied view.

explanations.title: Fixtures chosen to fail loudly
explanations.what: The shared view is asymmetric in latitude and longitude, and the Alaska bbox is the real one from the bundled boundaries.
explanations.why: A square fixture would let a predicate that swapped lat and lng, or dropped an axis entirely, pass by coincidence. Alaska is the live pathological case rather than a synthetic one.

explanations.title: Containment cases
explanations.what: Covers in-view, exactly filling, single-axis overflow, fully off-screen, unknown view, zero-area, Alaska, and views spelled wrapped, unwrapped and wider than a full turn.
explanations.why: The last three are not hypotheticals — they are the three spellings the engines actually emit, and each one has its own way of misclassifying a selection.

explanations.title: Anchor cases
explanations.what: Centroid kept when in view or when no view is given; view centre when off-screen in either axis, including on wrapped and overwide views.
explanations.why: Pins the two things the anchor must never do: move a perfectly good centroid, and place the fallback outside the view it was meant to rescue.

explanations.title: Bus mock and teardown
explanations.what: The mock resolves `map:getBounds` with the given view and records everything; fake timers run with `shouldAdvanceTime` so awaited flushes still resolve, and teardown clears timers, the mock and the tool's singleton state.
explanations.why: The fit path arms a 1500ms fallback timer that would otherwise outlive its test and fire into the next one, and `AOITool._state` is shared across every test in the file.

explanations.title: The two main paths
explanations.what: An in-view selection makes no `map:fitBounds` call, subscribes to no `moveend`, and mounts the tooltip at its own centroid; an overflowing one forwards the selection's extent and mounts only once the fallback fires.
explanations.why: These are the two halves of the issue's acceptance criteria, asserted at the bus boundary — the same place a real engine would see them — rather than through the helpers a second time.

explanations.title: Completion via moveend
explanations.what: Invokes the registered handler with the view-state payload `Map_` really re-emits, then checks the handler is unhooked and the disarmed fallback cannot mount a second tooltip.
explanations.why: Using the realistic payload is what makes this test able to catch the cross-file mistake the wrapper in AOITool guards against, rather than just asserting that some handler was called.

explanations.title: Degraded paths
explanations.what: A rejected `fitBounds` and an unframeable Alaska selection both end with the tooltip at the centre of the unchanged view.
explanations.why: Both are cases where the camera stays put with an off-screen centroid — the exact combination that would otherwise strand the selection with no reachable Analyze or Cancel.

overview.purpose: The existing unit suite for the deck.gl adapter, exercising it through a lightweight fake deck instance.

explanations.title: Rotation regression for getBounds
explanations.what: Adds a standalone-mode `getBounds` block: one test that the bounds bracket the centre, and one that half a turn of bearing returns the same envelope, still ordered south-west to north-east.
explanations.why: Bearing 180 is the cleanest probe — the two corners the old code read swap exactly — so the assertion pins the ordering without depending on the trigonometry of an arbitrary angle.

explanations.title: Wording-only comment rewrite
explanations.what: An unrelated test comment restated in plainer English.
explanations.why: Part of the branch's comment pass; nothing about the drawing-overlay tests changes.
